checks: Concavity and upper semicontinuity give compact convex transverse-symmetric section bodies, unit areas and both centroid coordinates zero. The lifted hull over -1 and 1 has exactly those extreme fibers and their exact Minkowski average at base zero. The cap s+alpha z≥0 has the specified signs for the two tails and keeps endpoint traces even when their length is zero.

At fixed knots the feasible heights form a compact polytope because each knot contributes with a positive coefficient to its profile's unit trapezoidal mass. The finitely many cross-slope comparisons partition it into closed cells.

For the upper Minkowski roof, assigning axial displacement to decreasing slopes maximizes the summed ordinate by exchanging lengths from a smaller filled slope to a larger unfilled one. Such a greedy allocation respects each input's ordered prefixes. Parallel ties add only collinear vertices. Hence fixed cells have fixed abscissae for the merged roof and affine ordinates, including at the initial endpoint.

Integration over s≥0 uses fixed cutting abscissae and interpolation fractions in each cell, and the endpoint tail integrations are also affine in their heights. Thus a minimizing cell vertex exists, even when the cut is a vertex or beyond the support.

After merging each within-profile collinear run, m+r+2 retained heights are free before the other active conditions. Positive-mass nonnegative concavity makes all interior knot heights positive. The four area/moment equations and z zero endpoint equations leave the stated lower bound, while cross-profile active equalities contribute at most min(m,r), since distinct slopes strictly decrease in each profile. A positive remaining dimension gives a two-sided segment in the same cell, contradicting vertexhood. This gives max(m,r)≤2+z; four prescribed endpoint equations give max(m,r)≤6.

Endpoint continuity follows from the one-sided concavity lower bound and upper semicontinuity upper bound. Uniform knot interpolation, normalization by mass and axial recentering produce exact constraints and support intervals converging to the given intervals. The mass bound gives height≤2/w by two supporting chords through a maximum point, including an endpoint maximum.

Passing to a subsequence of the at most seven upper vertices and their lower reflections yields Hausdorff-convergent hulls. The limit widths and convex-body indicators preserve mass and first moments, so the bodies remain full-dimensional. Lower reflections cannot add upper vertices and coincident abscissae can only collapse edges or give vertical end faces, keeping at most six nonvertical roof pieces.

Minkowski sums and all three fixed-halfplane areas converge, by Hausdorff continuity and null planar boundaries. The replacements therefore improve the original functional at the same alpha. No limit assertion about the original endpoint heights is used.

The mathematical scope matches original 92cf65df5512725a §§1–5. An independent rational check in the accepted rectangle specialization gives midpoint area 9/16, null left trace and right tail 3/4, hence J=21/16. This confirms the fixed-cap interpretation while the reviewed result makes no universal lower bound.

overlap.comparison: The centered unit-area rectangles at R=2 are a one-piece instance of the same actual fixed-tilt functional. This accepted counterexample at J=21/16 neither gives nor conflicts with the fixed-knot or arbitrary-profile replacement theorem.

readability: The finite rank bound is on the number of affine graph pieces in each profile, not on the total across both. Vertical support faces in the limit do not count as graph pieces.
review_method: Independent frozen-proof and source comparison with exact arithmetic where applicable
summary: The finite slope-order polytope and compactness of bounded polygonal replacements yield the exact six-piece fixed-tilt reduction for actual symmetric section bodies.
